narrative.overview:
Kimma.ai treats a candidate's background the way an archive treats a record. The surface is a cool, acid-free board (#f4f5f2, never cream) under a Hollinger blue-grey chrome bar; documents are white catalog cards with a red top rule; everything the AI marks is stamped in violet ink. The materials are the archive's own: stamps, slip markers, folder tabs, finding-aid outlines, typewriter readouts. The product refuses the AI-dashboard default (no glowing orb, no gradients, no score rings) and reads as a calm, precise place where a person can check the work.

Density is document-first. Exactly one document owns the desk at a time (a CV, a report, a ledger); folder tabs swap it hard, never tile it. Dense surfaces (transcript, ledger, evidence) keep one text size and get rank from weight, case, reversal and rule. The 24px card rule is the layout armature: ruled cards put every text row on a 24px baseline, and spacing moves in 12/24 steps.

Color is spent by meaning. Violet means the AI marked this. Red means a recording, and also the top rule of every catalog card. Ink buttons carry the one primary action per view. Nothing else is chromatic.
keyCharacteristics: Cool board, white cards, blue-grey chrome; one violet voice, one red voice.
Public Sans for reading, Courier Prime for call numbers, timecodes and readouts.
Flat surfaces with 1px rules; depth by tonal layering and a single sheet shadow.
Every record carries a call number (R-014, C-0388, Q2.3, T-118) in mono.
Only readouts and stamp presses move; everything else is still.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Violet is what the AI marked; red is a recording or a card's top rule. A human action, a status, or decoration never borrows either.

rules.name: The Cool Board Rule
rules.body: Backgrounds are blue-grey neutrals. Warm or cream grounds are out of the world.

rules.name: The One Size Rule
rules.body: Dense surfaces use 14px throughout. Rank comes from weight, case, reversal (a white-on-ink current line) and rule, never from stepping size.

rules.name: The Typewriter Rule
rules.body: Anything indexed, timed or counted is mono and tabular. Prose is never mono.

rules.name: The One Label Rule
rules.body: A question has one call tag (Q2.3) from questionLabel; no surface composes its own.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: Cards sit on the board with a rule, not a shadow. The sheet shadow belongs only to a document lifted onto the desk.

dos: **Do** use violet only for what the AI marked and red only for a recording or a catalog card's top rule.
**Do** put a mono call number on every record, quote and rating.
**Do** keep dense surfaces at 14px and rank by weight, case, reversal and rule.
**Do** align ruled cards to the 24px rule and space in 12/24 steps.
**Do** keep targets at 44px minimum (48px in the room) and a visible 2px violet focus ring (white on the header).
**Do** keep one primary ink button per view and confirm risky actions inline.
donts: **Don't** add gradients, glows, orbs, score rings or avatars; the AI is a stamp, not a persona.
**Don't** use warm or cream grounds, or hard offset shadows.
**Don't** make danger red; danger is an ink-2 border and weight.
**Don't** tile documents; one owns the desk and tabs hard-swap.
**Don't** animate anything except stamp presses, slip entry and readouts, and never past reduced-motion.
**Don't** treat the mono small-caps section labels (kicker line over a card, "FINDING AID", SERIES headings) as a pattern for new surfaces; see the note below.
